audit.whatIsWrong: Mocking Shout is never named in either layer, and its actual condition is never stated — the content layer just calls it 'W slow'.
audit.why: Riot's own text: enemies with their backs turned to Tryndamere also have their move speed reduced. The slow is conditional on facing. A Nasus who backs off in a straight line eats it; a Nasus who walks away while still facing Tryndamere does not get slowed at all. This is the single most abusable piece of tech in the matchup and it was absent.
audit.corrected: Mocking Shout only slows enemies whose backs are turned; disengage facing him. 14s cooldown.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tryndamere.json — W Mocking Shout description and cooldown

audit.whatIsWrong: Neither layer connects the other half of Mocking Shout — the attack-damage reduction — to Siphoning Strike.
audit.why: Mocking Shout decreases surrounding champions’ attack damage, and Siphoning Strike is an attack-damage-scaling empowered auto. So his W is not just a kite tool, it is a direct nerf to the one hit Nasus has spent the whole game building. Both layers describe Nasus as simply out-scaling him without noting the tax.
audit.corrected: Mocking Shout lowers the AD that Siphoning Strike scales off; it is up every 14s.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns listed only Undying Rage and gave no per-rank numbers for anything.
audit.why: Undying Rage is a 120/100/80s ultimate — you cannot plan a lane around it. Spinning Slash at 12/11/10/9/8s and Mocking Shout at 14s are the cooldowns that actually gate his commits.
audit.corrected: Mocking Shout with its facing condition added, Undying Rage given real numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers treat a low-health Tryndamere as a nearly-dead one; nothing warns that his damage goes up as he drops.
audit.why: Battle Fury builds crit chance from attacks and kills, and Bloodlust increases his attack damage the more wounded he is before he spends Fury to heal. So the moment a Nasus feels the duel turning is exactly the moment Tryndamere is at his strongest, which is how the coin-flip all-in gets lost.
audit.corrected: A low Tryndamere is the dangerous one; Bloodlust converts missing health into AD and then heals it back every 12s.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tryndamere.json — P Battle Fury, Q Bloodlust

audit.whatIsWrong: winCon and dosFull[2] both say "anti-heal" but no layer names Grievous Wounds or a timing.
audit.why: Bloodlust is his only sustain and it is on a 12s cooldown with no mana cost, so the healing arrives in every extended trade for free. Nasus grinds with Soul Eater lifesteal; the fight is decided by which side’s healing is answered.
audit.corrected: Bloodlust named with its cooldown so the reader knows what to cut; the item timing still belongs in the itemization block inside report[].

audit.whatIsWrong: The full-layer chart gives Tryndamere stages 1-4; the content chart gives him only stages 1-2 and calls 3-4 Skill.
audit.why: Nasus wins 54.14% over 652 games and Wither is a point-and-click answer to an attack-speed duellist with one dash.
audit.corrected: phases[2].side and phases[3].side should read Skill. Not edited: "Tryndamere" is 10 characters against "Skill" at 5, so the ±10% band rejects the token swap.

edits.before: Wither online — it's your get-off-me button, not a kill tool yet. Hold it for Tryndamere's engage, never open with it.
edits.after: Mocking Shout cuts your attack damage, and Siphoning Strike scales off AD — his W is a damage nerf on your one big hit.

edits.before: E lets you stack safely from range when Tryndamere zones you. Spirit Fire the wave under tower; every stack denied is his only real win condition.
edits.after: Wither is online. Mocking Shout only slows enemies whose backs are turned, so walk away still facing him and the slow never applies to you.

edits.before: Still Tryndamere's window — respect Undying Rage fully. Passive lifesteal plus Fleet means he must commit hard to actually dent you; make those commits cost.
edits.after: Spinning Slash is 12s at rank 1 — that is your window. Bloodlust turns his missing health into attack damage, so a low Trynd is the dangerous one, not the safe one.

edits.before: Fury of the Sands flips dives: pop R, Wither Tryndamere, and suddenly the stat-check runs your way. First real fight you're allowed to take.
edits.after: Undying Rage makes burst pointless — pop Fury of the Sands, Wither his attack speed, and just outlast the window where he cannot die.

edits.before: - Tryndamere Undying Rage: matchup-defining — Unkillable 5s. Wither him after it. Track it before every engage.
edits.after: - Tryndamere Mocking Shout: 14s — its slow only lands if your back is turned. - Tryndamere Undying Rage: 120/100/80s.

edits.before: Unkillable 5s. Wither him after it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: He cannot die while it is up — Wither him and simply wait it out instead.

edits.before: Tryndamere wastes Undying Rage — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Bloodlust turns his stacked Fury into a heal on a 12s cooldown.

edits.before: Burning your answer for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Turning your back is exactly what arms Mocking Shout's move-speed slow.

edits.before: Wither lands at 3 and zeroes his attack speed and move speed, but he still wins extended trades on its cooldown — it's a coin-flip.
edits.after: Wither at 3 guts his attack speed, but Mocking Shout still cuts the AD your Siphoning Strike scales off — call it a coin-flip.

edits.before: Use E gap-close plus W slow to all-in you whenever Wither is on cooldown
edits.after: Use Spinning Slash plus a Mocking Shout slow while your back is turned

notes: I deliberately did not restate the '5 seconds' duration the existing dosFull text gives for Undying Rage — the kit file carries cooldowns but not durations, so I wrote around it rather than repeating an unverified number. The existing 'Unkillable 5s' line is being replaced anyway.
